newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Native groups charge their cultures are exploited.
newsitem.headline: Native groups charge their cultures are exploited.

text.p: Indigenous groups from around the world charged on Monday that conservation efforts have so far failed to safeguard their cultures.

"Our knowledge, innovations and practices are extracted from us without our consent for the purpose of commercial use," the International Indigenous Forum said in a statement to delegates from 162 countries at the start of the Second Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biodiversity.
"Our rights as peoples to self-determination, among others, are not recognised," the forum said.

"The issue of biodiversity and the collective rights of indigenous peoples cannot be separated," the meeting, which opened over the weekend, said on Monday. The convention, drafted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, aims to protect the diversity of life on the planet.
Officials argue that it is making good progress in promoting native peoples's rights but say it is a limited tool and should not be expected to become too broad-ranging.
"This is a convention about biological diversity, it is not a convention about human rights," Calestous Juma, executive secretary of the convention, told Reuters.

"That is why it cannot deal explicitly with self-determination. But it deals with protection of the knowledge, practices and innovations of indigenous and local communities, aspects which are very closely linked to the identity of people, and it makes an important contribution there," Juma said.

Native groups fear that without new provisions, prospecting by multinational firms for rare forms of plant life and other materials will continue unchecked. "We are the guardians of these territories which have the greatest diversity of life," indigenous forum spokesman Eusebio Condori told Reuters.

"We must stop the invasion of scientists who go house by house in our communities, trying to extract all the knowledge we have had for so many years and which we have shared with the white man for free. At this rate, one day we may have to pay for our own medicine."
